speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a longstanding pruritic rash accompanied by numbness and tingling in your palms. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any specific shape or pattern to the rash, such as red rings or concentric circles?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That exposure to livestock and farming is significant; have you noticed any red spots or blisters on your skin, particularly around your mouth or eyes, or any swollen lymph nodes in your neck or armpits?

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial labs and imaging are normal, which helps rule out acute systemic infections. Given your history of farming, livestock contact, and the combination of a pruritic rash with sensory changes in the palms, I need to clarify if you have noticed any ulcers, scabs, or nodules on your hands or face, and if you have had any difficulty breathing or joint pain.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on upper body and face. I also have Numbness and tingling sensation of both palms, Thinning of the eyebrows, Loss of some eyelashes, Hypopigmented macules around the elbows.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (specifically Leishmaniasis Recidivans or diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis) given the triad of pruritic rash, sensory disturbances (numbness/tingling) in palms, and hypopigmented macules on elbows. The numbness suggests nerve involvement often seen in chronic or disseminated forms, while the eyebrow/eyelash thinning and hypopigmentation are characteristic skin findings.
